name: Pull a target
summary: Grab one enemy with a hook, a beam or a psychic grip and move it against its will: drag it to you, haul it toward your team, lift it into the air, or take it out of its formation or over a wall. While held, the target usually can't move or fire, and a lifted ground target often becomes something anti-air can shoot. The pull itself may do little harm; the payoff is where the target ends up: in front of your guns or under your treads, over water or a drop, or within reach of your teammates. It is usually one target at a time, with a visible throw or beam (hooks can be dodged; most RTS beams and grips lock on), and the puller is busy or rooted while it holds. Pushing targets away is the knockback weapon trait; taking over a target's actions is mind control.
counterplay: Dodge the throw or break line of sight before the pull starts; hooks and beams are visible and often loud.
Stay beyond its reach, or get inside its minimum range: some pullers can't grab a target right next to them.
Hit the puller while it holds: it is rooted or silent, and killing or stunning it ends the pull at once.
Bring units it can't grab, such as soldiers against a vehicle-only beam, or aircraft in flight.
Have a teammate pull or shield the victim back out, or body-block the hook with someone tougher.
Keep away from water, edges and hazards where a drop does the killing.

other_examples.note: A super-heavy tank's second weapon hauls ground vehicles and ships to it and grinds them under its own extra treads; against buildings and bigger units it drags itself to them instead, and a target that can't be dragged because something blocks the way is destroyed outright. Using it puts the slow tank in the line of fire, and a later patch stopped it moving while it harpoons.

sources.title: Apocalypse tank (Red Alert 3), Command & Conquer Wiki

other_examples.note: Her basic attack lifts a ground unit and holds it helpless while damage piles up, and anti-air weapons can hit it while it hangs; fliers are dragged to the ground instead. She must focus on one target at a time, but the disable lingers for a few seconds after she moves on, so a skilled player can keep several enemies up at once.

Pulls any one unit, friend or foe, to the viper's location, even up or down cliffs, so it can rescue an ally or pluck an enemy out of position; the pulled unit can't attack on the way, heroic units are immune, and the viper is briefly frozen after the cast.

Lifts one ground unit so that it can't move, attack or use abilities, and anti-air weapons can hit it while it floats; the phoenix can't move or attack while it holds the beam, and the lift ends if either of them dies.

sources.title: Graviton Beam ability box, StarCraft Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: A thrown chain drags one enemy hero into shotgun range. The victim goes free if it gets out of sight in the brief moment before the pull begins, the hook ends if Roadhog is stunned, and a support hero's own pull can yank the victim back out.

A long skillshot hook, aimed at a point, catches the first unit in its path, friend or foe, and drags it back over trees and cliffs. Both teams hear the throw, even when the thrower is hidden from sight, and Pudge is locked in place while the hook flies out.

player_translation.summary: A skillshot hook or a held beam aimed with the mouse: hit an enemy and it is hauled toward you, or lifted and helpless, for a moment, then set down where you choose, in your team's guns or over a hazard. You are rooted while you hold, and a missed throw leaves you waiting for the cooldown.
as_user: The skill is aim and timing: the hook flies along a visible line and grabs the first enemy it meets. Lead moving targets and catch the one standing out of position.
On a hit you hold the pull for a short moment. Your own gun is silent and you can't move, so pull when your team can cover you.

The payoff is where the target lands: at your feet in front of your team, behind a wall away from its friends, or over a hazard. In the lift variant a held enemy becomes an air target for your anti-air teammates.
Weight matters: light targets come to you, while a target much heavier than you pulls you to it instead (the heavy-reel variant), which turns the hook into a gap closer.
as_target: The throw shows and sounds: sidestep it, break line of sight or duck behind cover during the wind-up.
Once hooked you can't fire during the short pull. A lift lasts longer, so hold F to struggle free sooner and call for help.
Being dropped hurts only where the map makes it hurt (water, hazards, falling onto units), and those spots are marked.
After a pull you are briefly immune to the next one.
teammates: The puller's team: a classic setup for a finisher. Anti-air teammates punish a lifted target, and a mind-controller or a heavy tank waits where the target lands.
The target's team: shoot or stun the rooted puller to cut the pull, body-block the hook with a tougher teammate, or pull the victim back with your own hook.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse fires your main weapon.
Q: throw the hook toward the cursor; on a hit the target is reeled in automatically. One counted key.
Lift variants: hold Q on a target to lift it, move the cursor to steer where it will be set down, and release to drop it.
Victim, with the universal keys: hold F to break a lift early; a short hook pull can't be broken.
feedback: A chain or beam drawn from puller to target, a throw sound both teams hear and a clank on a hit.
A landing marker on the ground under a lifted target, and a shadow that grows and shrinks so its height reads from above.
Water, edges and hazards light up when a lifted target is held over them.
A cooldown ring under the puller, and a 'hooked' banner with a direction arrow on the victim's HUD.
changes_from_rts: The Magnetron's beam locks on automatically; here the hook is a skillshot with travel time, so the target can dodge.
RTS lifts last as long as the beam is held; a person held in the air can't play, so lifts are capped at a few seconds and the victim can struggle.
Instant kills from dropping a vehicle into water or onto a building work against computer units but are harsh on a player; here drops deal heavy damage only over marked hazards.
Add an immunity window after each pull, so two pullers can't juggle one victim.
The Magnetron can't hurt soldiers at all; a player version keeps a light gun so it isn't helpless between hooks.
The server must decide pulls with lag compensation, or hooks will snap victims from where they no longer stand.

team_play.notes: The pull is a setup that only pays if a teammate converts it (guns, anti-air, a controller waiting where the target lands); the ally-rescue variant lets the same hook save a teammate.

notes: A projectile followed by forced movement is a solved problem in hero shooters.
Dragging through the map needs rules for walls, cliffs, other units and water (StarCraft II's Abduct even pulls up and down cliffs).
Weight classes decide who moves toward whom.
Interactions with stasis, shields, invulnerability, vehicles carrying passengers and riders who bail out mid-pull.
Server authority and lag compensation for skillshots.
A pull straight into a waiting team is close to a guaranteed kill; cooldown, travel time and the miss chance are the levers.
Environmental kills (water, cliffs, landing on units) can be too strong; keep them to marked hazards.
Several pullers chaining one victim; the post-pull immunity fixes it.
Height is hard to read from above, so lifted targets need a shadow and a landing marker.
In a crowd, who is pulling whom must be obvious.

variants.name: Hook and drag
variants.summary: A thrown hook drags the first enemy it hits back to you, with light damage and a short moment of helplessness.
variants.seen_in: Dota 2 Pudge, Overwatch Roadhog, Red Alert 3 Apocalypse Tank harpoon

variants.name: Lift and hold
variants.summary: Hold a beam to lift a target: it can't move or fire and counts as an air target; releasing the beam drops it.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Magnetron, StarCraft II Phoenix, Red Alert 3 Yuriko Omega

variants.name: Haul and set down
variants.summary: Carry a lifted target toward you or over a wall and set it down on a spot you choose, such as next to a teammate who can finish or capture it.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Magnetron (hauls vehicles toward Yuri's mind-controllers and across walls)

variants.name: Ally rescue
variants.summary: The same pull works on teammates, to yank a friend out of danger.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Viper's Abduct, Dota 2 Pudge's hook on allies

variants.name: Hazard drop
variants.summary: Dropping a lifted target over water, a ledge or onto other enemies deals heavy damage to it and to whatever it lands on.

variants.name: Heavy reel
variants.summary: Against targets heavier than you, the hook pulls you to them instead, which makes it a gap closer.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 3 Apocalypse Tank against buildings and bigger units

variants.name: Grinder hold
variants.summary: Drag a vehicle under your own treads or blades and keep hurting it for as long as it is held.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 3 Apocalypse Tank grinder treads

variants.name: Lingering juggle
variants.summary: The disable lasts a few seconds after you let go, so you can lift several enemies in turn.

adds_strengths.why: Pulls one enemy out of its group and into your team's guns, behind a wall or up into the air where it can't fight back.

adds_weaknesses.why: One target at a time; it stands still and holds fire while it pulls, and a missed throw leaves it waiting.

counters.why: Artillery hiding behind its front line is dragged into brawling range.
Snipers holding a far sightline are hooked off it.
Lone vehicles are lifted out of the fight or hauled away from their escort.

countered_by.why: Quick targets sidestep the hook and close in while it is on cooldown.
A stun on the rooted puller cuts the pull short.
Long-range fire hits the puller from beyond the reach of its hook.

open_questions: Should a lift turn a ground target into an air target for anti-air, as in Red Alert 2 and StarCraft II?
How harsh should map hazards be when a lifted target is dropped over them?
May the hook grab teammates, and can a tougher teammate body-block it?

shooter_fit.reason: Hooks are proven in hero shooters and top-down games (Roadhog, Pudge): a skillshot with a clear tell, a dodge window and a big team payoff.
